tracks.title: Static
tracks.loreNote: The opening statement of the "Freedom Era." Recorded in the warehouse with amps turned to 11, this track acts as a direct rejection of the "hollow sound" Apex forced the band to make for five years. The line "I am the static! I am the noise!" became the rallying cry for the "Ironhead" fanbase during the band's independent rebirth.

tracks.title: Garbage
tracks.loreNote: Ryan's raw, "jangle-rock" rage track. It retells the infamous "dirty mirror" incident from the 1992 *Friction* photo shoot, where an executive tried to offer him cocaine on a mirror, and Ryan—innocently thinking it was dirt—wiped it clean with a napkin. The song channels his fury at the executive who humiliated him and tried to destroy his family.

tracks.title: Not Your Saint
tracks.loreNote: After the "Tabloid Hell" of the 1994 trial, the media tried to paint Cassidy as a "Victim-Saint"—a fragile, broken doll. This fierce arena anthem is her rejection of that narrative. She is neither the "Stardust" pop star nor the "Victim" of the scandal; she is a rock musician standing on her own two feet.

tracks.title: Atmosphere
tracks.loreNote: The "Lost Gem" from the canceled 1992 *Friction* sessions. The band wrote this song about the literal, scientific friction of a space shuttle re-entering Earth's atmosphere ("Here comes the friction / Feel the fire"). The "rogue" executive, Julian Vance, misinterpreted these lyrics as sexual metaphors, leading to the catastrophic misunderstanding that destroyed the contract. This is the original 1992 demo, released here for the first time.

tracks.title: The Fortress
tracks.loreNote: The epic closer of Side A. This arena-rock anthem is dedicated to the "Ironheads" and CPI alumni who funded the band's freedom through the "Forger Nation War Chest." The "Fortress" is both their warehouse studio and the protective wall their fans built around them.

tracks.title: Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)
tracks.loreNote:
The "Magnum Opus" that consumes the entirety of Side B. This 15-minute progressive rock suite is Cassidy O'Connell's autobiographical journey from the trauma of the trial ("The Cage") to the transcendence of artistic freedom ("The Cosmos").

Known by fans simply as **"Ad Astra,"** the track features a distinct "mechanical cutoff" sound between Part II and Part III, created by Ryan pulling the plug on his guitar amp to simulate a rocket's Main Engine Cutoff (MECO).
